messages:
maria: Heads up — p99 for /generate on model-redwood/v8.2 jumped to ~420ms right after this morning's rollout. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/latency-route (canary ~50% traffic).

deploy-bot: rolled out model-redwood/v8.2 to canary (50%) at 2167889000 :rocket:

devon: Is this across hosts or concentrated? brief numbers pls

maria: Concentrated on shard-12 and shard-13. Overall throughput dipped ~18%. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~420ms.

kai: Any KV cache numbers? could be cache churn from tokenizer change

maria: KV stats snippet from shard-12 profiler:
```
kvcache.stats host=shard-12
hit_rate: 0.86 -> 0.44
evictions_per_s: 20 -> 120
avg_seq_len: 152 -> 280
cache_size_bytes: stable
```

anita: wow avg_seq_len doubled for the same workload? that smells like tokenization differences

devon: grabbed a couple of sample requests pre/post rollout — same prompt: old_tokens=32, v8.2_tokens=67. Seems subtoken splitting increased dramatically.

maria: exact. tokenizer merge table changed in v8.2 (unknown token handling). That increases KV cache misses and long sequences => batcher chooses different kernels and triggers fallback to slower int8 path.

runtime-ci: alert: kernel_selector.fallback_count(host=shard-12) increased by 7x at 2167890005.

kai: Also seeing host-level GPU scheduling context switches — noisy tenant on shard-13: extra long-running profiling spans from tenant 'ad-hoc-eval' at 2167889500. nvidia-smi shows multiple small contexts.

ops: Could be 2 orthogonal causes that amplify: tokenizer-caused seqlen shift + noisy-tenant causing kernel scheduling delays and prefetcher eviction.

devon: quick perf flame graph (trimmed):
```
50% samples: attention_kernel_fast
p95: attention_kernel_slow (fallback)
p99: prefetcher_eviction -> kvcache.fetch_miss -> kernel_fallback
```

maria: hypothesis: increased seqlen pushes more requests into larger batch buckets, batcher heuristic flips kernel choice to fallback path due to memory pressure, while kvcache prefetcher tries to prefetch for longer sequences causing cache thrash.

anita: if prefetcher is aggressive for long seqs, it might evict useful prefixes for other requests on same host. combination => miss storm.

ops: mitigation options: 1) throttle canary down to 10% 2) pin canary hosts to non-noisy tenant hosts 3) rollback tokenizer change 4) tune prefetcher to cap prefetch window for v8.2

devon: I can push a quick runtime hotfix to cap prefetch window to 64 tokens on canary hosts — low risk.

maria: sounds good. also recommend forcing kernel selection policy to prefer stable kernel for seqlen>200 for now.

runtime-ci: triggered automated canary-slowdown: set traffic to 10% at 2167890150 :white_check_mark:

kai: started pinning canary to quieter hosts and isolating noisy tenant run.

maria: after slowdown + prefetch cap: shard-12 p99 dropped to ~210ms within 3 minutes. KV hit_rate recovered to 0.71. throughput back up ~8%.

ops: good. action items:
- devon to land prefetch cap + kernel selection tweak to canary (in progress)
- anita to open tokenizer regression ticket against model-redwood/v8.2 tokenizer merge table
- infra to audit noisy tenant scheduling on impacted hosts

anita: opening ticket RN with samples and repro steps. linking tokenizer diff and sample token counts. :memo:

devon: will follow up with perf numbers post-fix and propose a rollback if anything regresses.

maria: thanks everyone. marking this thread for postmortem if we end up rolling back. :eyes:
